chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who breached a house and was seized before he reached anything. He said: “He is to be punished; but if he is seized after having taken something out of it, then amputation applies to him.”

He said: And I asked him about a man whom they caught carrying a bale of clothes, and he said, “The owner of the house gave them to me.” He said: “Amputation is averted from him unless clear proof is established against him; if clear proof is established against him, he is amputated.”
And he said: “The hand and the foot are amputated, then after that he is not amputated again; rather, if he repeats, he is imprisoned and maintained from the treasury of the Muslims.”

key_terms.الْقَطْعُ: amputation as the prescribed hadd penalty for theft
key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury of the Muslims
key_terms.كَارَةً: a bale or bundle, here a load of garments
key_terms.نَقَبَ: broke into or breached a house by making an opening
key_terms.يُدْرَأُ: it is averted or warded off
key_terms.يُعَاقَبُ: he is punished with a discretionary punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on attempted theft, disputed stolen property, and repeat theft in Shiʿi hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning theft, attempted burglary, evidentiary doubt, and repeated offenses. It distinguishes between mere unlawful entry and completed theft, and it affirms that the hadd punishment is averted in the presence of a plausible claim unless proof is established. It also states the ruling for repeat offenders after prior amputation, including imprisonment and maintenance from the public treasury.
